NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute value chain, designing the world's most sought-after GPU accelerators while relying entirely on TSMC's advanced nodes (particularly CoWoS packaging for HBM integration) and a concentrated pool of HBM memory suppliers — making its supply chain highly capable but geographically concentrated in Taiwan. On the demand side, NVIDIA is overwhelmingly driven by hyperscalers and cloud providers racing to build AI infrastructure, with Microsoft, Meta, Google, and Amazon collectively representing an estimated 40-50% of Data Center segment revenues.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a fabless designer that outsources semiconductor manufacturing to TSMC and component sourcing to dozens of Asian suppliers, while maintaining tight vertical integration over software, silicon architecture, and retail. On the downstream side, Apple's scale and platform dominance give it enormous leverage over carriers, app developers, and digital advertising partners who depend on iOS access to reach over 1 billion active device users.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits in the middle of the semiconductor memory value chain, heavily dependent on a concentrated group of capital equipment suppliers (ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research) for its vertically integrated DRAM and NAND manufacturing. On the demand side, Micron is increasingly exposed to AI-driven hyperscaler and GPU customers — particularly NVIDIA for HBM — alongside traditional consumer electronics and cloud infrastructure buyers, making it a bellwether for both cyclical memory markets and secular AI infrastructure buildout.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM occupies a uniquely asset-light position at the apex of the semiconductor IP ecosystem, monetizing its CPU/GPU architecture designs through licensing fees and per-chip royalties rather than manufacturing anything itself, making its upstream dependencies primarily software tools (EDA) and cloud infrastructure rather than physical materials. Its downstream relationships span virtually every major chip designer globally — from mobile SoC vendors like Apple and Qualcomm to data center players like NVIDIA and Broadcom — giving ARM unparalleled leverage but also concentrated royalty risk in the smartphone and hyperscaler markets.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology operates as a fabless semiconductor company, sitting between upstream foundry and IP partners (primarily TSMC for advanced node manufacturing and Arm for processor IP) and a diversified set of downstream customers spanning hyperscale cloud providers, networking OEMs, and storage companies. Its strategic pivot toward custom AI ASICs and high-speed data center networking silicon has made hyperscalers like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft increasingly central to its revenue growth trajectory.
